title: Azure Cache for Redis Overview
description: Learn how Azure Cache for Redis provides in-memory caching to speed up applications and reduce database load.

data.text: Azure Cache for Redis is a fully managed in-memory data store based on the open-source Redis engine. It stores frequently accessed data in memory instead of a slower database, reducing latency and cutting down on expensive database queries. It supports strings, hashes, lists, sets, and pub/sub messaging.

data.title: What Developers Use Redis For
items: **Application cache** — store session state, API responses, or computed results.
**Leaderboards and counters** — atomic increment operations are fast and thread-safe.
**Rate limiting** — track request counts per user or IP in Redis.

rows: Single node, no SLA, no persistence

data.title: Cache Aside Pattern
data.text: The most common pattern: check the cache first, fall back to the database on a miss, then write the result back to the cache. This keeps the cache warm without complex synchronization.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Cached API Response
data.description: Add Redis caching to an existing API endpoint.
steps: Provision an Azure Cache for Redis instance.
Add StackExchange.Redis to an ASP.NET Core project.
Create a middleware or action filter that checks Redis before calling the database.
On a cache miss, query the database and store the result with a 5-minute TTL.
Test with repeated requests and confirm the second request hits the cache.
data.expectedOutcome: An API endpoint that serves cached responses and reduces database load.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Cache for Redis is a fully managed Redis service.
It reduces latency and database load by storing hot data in memory.
Choose Basic for dev/test, Standard for production, and Premium for mission-critical.
The Cache Aside pattern is the simplest way to start using Redis.
data.takeaway: Redis is one of the most impactful performance tools in any cloud application.
